mechanisms.description: A trust-extension order extends the trust period on named allotments, or on all allotments whose period expires in a stated year or on a stated date, for a stated number of years. Its operation ends when that extended period runs out.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Stated expiry year (or date) plus the stated number of years; an interval covering the calendar year(s) in which the extended periods end, widened to the order date plus the period where the text does not say the extension runs from expiry.

mechanisms.description: IRA sec. 2 (1934) extended and continued every trust period then running "until otherwise directed by Congress", except for the Oklahoma tribes listed in sec. 13 and reservations that voted to exclude themselves under sec. 18. It continues the trust by statute; it does not name, amend or continue any executive order, and it is not an end of one.

For reservations that voted to exclude themselves from the IRA, the Act of June 15, 1935, sec. 3, extended unextended trust periods to December 31, 1936; later blanket orders (EO 7464 and its annual successors to EO 10191) and Interior orders to 1988 extended them further. Each is a new instrument running from the expiry of the period it extends.

A temporary withdrawal "until" a stated date, in aid of proposed legislation, ends on that date by its own terms (the lands then "become subject to disposal ... without further order"), or earlier if Congress legislates or the President directs otherwise.
A later executive order that names the member and cancels, revokes or supersedes it ends it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of the later order.

mechanisms.description: An order whose only command restores lands to the public domain, eliminates lands from a reservation, amends or partly revokes another order, or confirms a single entry is spent on issue as a command; its effect is evidence for the lifecycle of the order or reservation it changed.

From 1919-06-30 no new executive-order reservation could be made, and from 1927-03-03 the boundaries of executive-order reservations could be changed only by Act of Congress. A standing reservation order therefore persists until a later executive order (before 1927-03-03) or a statute changes or ends it; these statutes end nothing themselves and tell where to look.

A regulation in force on the cutoff that identifies the reservation as the one the order established is a current-law predicate that the order's operative effect, the reservation, was in force on 2026-10-14.

lead.basis: A reservation order continues until a later order (before 1927-03-03) or a statute changes or ends it; after 1927-03-03 only an Act of Congress could change its boundaries. No class-wide event ended these reservations, and no held current-law record shows them in force.

gaps: Per reservation: later statutes confirming, enlarging, diminishing, terminating or restoring these lands (Statutes at Large, U.S. Code title 25 notes), and a current predicate (statute, regulation or BIA land record) for the lands on 2026-10-14.
Kappler IV (held, to 1927) prints the later orders for these reservations and is the place to check for pre-1927 executive changes.

lead.basis: No branch fits the order as held.

gaps: Individual review.
